review:
I read the on-disk source rather than trusting the paste. The pasted PRIMARY EDITION matches `human-review/gwt-response/main.tex` byte-for-byte through the truncation point, so the paste is faithful. The twin was not provided, and I could not reach the published-research copy — see §3.

---

VERDICT: REJECTED

---

## Findings

### 1. CRITICAL — The headline AUROC carries the wrong FWL label, and the wrong range with it

**Location:** `gwt-response/main.tex` abstract L84, intro L136–137, §2.2 L205–206.

> `$0.707$~(FWL, permutation $p{=}0.001$)`
> `AUROC ranges from $0.627$--$0.999$ across designs; the cleanest post-audit number is $0.707$ (FWL-corrected, permutation $p{=}0.001$, Oracle Loop)`

**Why it is wrong.** The correction is recorded in a primary source *in the same directory*, `gwt-response/cache_tracing_report.tex` L14–15, a banner Lyra wrote on 2026-08-15:

> `%%   - confab AUROC 0.707 -> 0.620 with FWL (0.707 without); range`
> `%%     0.627--0.999 -> 0.620--0.999`

Independently confirmed in `convergence-paper/main.tex` L181–182: *"AUROC 0.620 after FWL residualization, 0.707 without FWL; range 0.620–0.999."* And L310–311 of that same file gives the p-values: `0.620` carries permutation `p=0.023`; `0.707` carries `p=0.001`. This paper took the **non-FWL** number, kept the **non-FWL** p-value, and pinned the **FWL** label on both. This is not a rounding slip — it upgrades the paper's cleanest post-audit statistic from "weak but real after confound removal" to "survives confound removal at p=0.001," which is the entire load-bearing claim of the abstract.

**Fix.** Three edits: abstract L84 → `$0.620$~(FWL, permutation $p{=}0.023$; $0.707$ without FWL, $p{=}0.001$)`. Intro L136 and §2.2 L205 → range `$0.620$--$0.999$`. §2.2 L206 → `$0.620$ (FWL-corrected, permutation $p{=}0.023$)`. Then add a visible dated correction note in the same form `convergence-paper` L188–198 already uses — do not fix silently; this paper is cited by `meta-pattern` as `lyra2026gwt_response`, and readers of that citation need to see what moved.

**Attribution also diverges:** this paper sources `0.707` to `\citep{lyra2026oracle}`; both sibling files source the confab AUROC to `\citep{lyra2026decision}`. Resolve which.

---

### 2. CRITICAL — "killed finding #4" points at a row index that rotted when the table was replaced

**Location:** §7.2 "Internal disagreements," L739–740.

> `our own killed finding \#4 (depth reorganization generic to any instruction pair) predicts high overlap generically`

**Why it is wrong.** Row 4 of Table~\ref{tab:bodycount} is *"Same-prompt deception — Length-only; input\_auc=1.0."* It has nothing to do with depth reorganization or instruction pairs. The paper itself explains why (§6, L560–563): *"An earlier draft of this paper substituted a different set of ten kills chosen for their fit with the workspace narrative; the canonical list includes length-confound kills..."* — the ten rows were swapped wholesale, and this pointer was never re-aimed. The finding it names is not in the canonical table at all. This is the exact index-rot failure class: a reference to a *position* in a table rather than to a *row*.

**Second rotted pointer, same cause.** §3.4 L408: `may reflect generic instruction-pair overlap (see \S\ref{sec:bodycount})`. §6 and Table 2 contain no discussion of the 0.972 overlap, no null distribution over instruction pairs, and no depth-reorganization kill. The cross-reference resolves to a section that does not contain the caveat it promises.

**Fix.** Replace `killed finding \#4` with the row's name and its kill reason as they appear in the canonical list — and if "depth reorganization generic to any instruction pair" is a real kill, it is missing from Table 2 and must be added or the sentence dropped. Retarget the §3.4 `\S\ref{sec:bodycount}` pointer to wherever the null-distribution caveat actually lives (currently: nowhere). Institute the rule for both: name the row, never the index.

---

### 3. CRITICAL — Retracted numbers shipped as a live "suspected finding"

**Location:** §6, L554–555.

> `(5)~discrete emotion identity in single-turn settings (Qwen L3 $= 2.8\times$, Mistral L4 $= 2.5\times$, scoped to single-turn only)`

**Why it is wrong.** `cache_tracing_report.tex` L9–11:

> `%%   - 'user-emotion encoding (2.5--2.8x signal)': RETRACTED 2026-05-21,`
> `%%     dropped upstream (survivor is W_K DIRECTIONAL, and this sentence`
> `%%     is explicitly scoped to spectral measurements)`

`convergence-paper` L189–194 gives the mechanism: *"retracted at its source on 2026-05-21 as an FWL-before-CV leakage artifact; the surviving result is the $W_K$ directional probe at $12.3\times$ chance, and the spectral probe for emotion is at chance."* Corroborated twice independently: `empathy-bus/paper.md` L56 (*"W_K projection reads 30-class user emotion at 12.3× chance"*), and `contextual-engagement-paper/main.tex` L378 (*"emotion identity is not encoded in shape at all"*).

I checked the disambiguation the banner warns about — L17–18 says the *"2.3–2.8x tail smear"* figures are a different, still-valid measurement, "do not bulk-edit on 2.8." This is not that: same numbers, same early layers, same models, same instrument scope.

**Fix.** Delete suspected-finding (5). If a single-turn emotion-identity claim is to survive, restate it as the $W_K$ directional probe at $12.3\times$ chance and state that the spectral probe is at chance — which materially weakens §3 and §5.1, because a spectral instrument that is at chance on emotion undercuts "V-projection geometry reads workspace state."

---

### 4. CRITICAL — `0.154` vs `0.080` was removed upstream as unsourceable; it appears here four times and is load-bearing

**Location:** §2.2 L234–239, §3.4 L387–390, §3.6 L433, §7.2 L736.

`cache_tracing_report.tex` L12–13: `%% - 'distinctiveness 0.154 vs substrate 0.080': appears NOWHERE in the cited paper; unsourceable, removed upstream`. `convergence-paper` L195–198: *"they come from an internal analysis that has not been published, so the citation could not be followed. Both have been removed rather than re-sourced."*

This paper re-points the number at `\citep{lyra2026portrait}` — an `@unpublished` entry, *"Vera's Geometric Birthday Portrait,"* with no URL, no DOI, no archive locator. That converts an unsourceable number into an unverifiable one; it does not fix it. The paper's own §2.2 concedes *"No statistics reported; the null distribution of instruction-pair overlaps has not been established"* — and then §3.6 L433–437 builds an argument on it anyway (*"is not merely 'context establishing a persona' — it is workspace content shaping downstream reasoning"*), and §5 lists it under "cross-scale universality / practical intervention" contributions.

**Fix.** Either ship `lyra2026portrait` as a citable artifact with the measurement and its null, or remove the pair everywhere and delete the §3.6 CRT-analogy paragraph that rests on it. Do not carry an unpublished internal measurement as evidence in a venue-facing paper.

---

### 5. MAJOR — There is no rendered artifact. The paper has never been built.

`find gwt-response -iname "*.pdf" -o -iname "*.aux" -o -iname "*.bbl"` returns nothing. Every one of the fifteen other papers in `human-review/` has a `main.pdf`. `.gitignore` does **not** ignore `*.pdf` (it ignores `.aux/.log/.bbl` etc., which is why the absence of those is expected and the absence of the PDF is not). `ACTIVE_REVIEW.md` L34–35 states the ten intake papers were moved *"(sources + PDFs, build artifacts dropped)"* — this one arrived without one.

This is worse than STALE_PDF: there is no evidence the source compiles. Given finding #11 below, it probably compiles with an undefined-citation warning.

**Fix.** Build it. Confirm zero undefined references and zero undefined citations in `main.log` before any further review.

---

### 6. MAJOR — The "we dropped six rows" note contradicts the table it sits under

**Location:** L306–314, immediately after Table 1.

> `We dropped six rows from an earlier draft that did not survive adversarial review: mid-layer localization and scale invariance (expected under any trained-network account), ...`

Table 1 still contains the row `Workspace in intermediate layers | Metacognitive features strongest mid-to-deep | Mid-layer localization of abstract structure is generic; not workspace-specific`, filed under **Expected**. Mid-layer localization was *reclassified*, not dropped. The arithmetic depends on it: twelve original rows minus six dropped = six remaining, and the table has exactly six rows — which only balances if this row is gone. Either the note or the table is wrong.

**Second half of the same defect:** the note says the consciousness-deflection row was dropped because its `0.972` overlap *"lacks a null distribution over arbitrary instruction pairs."* That row is gone from Table 1 — and the claim survives verbatim in prose at §3.4 L402–410, presented as *"consistent with our finding that consciousness deflection instructions are geometrically shallow."* A finding removed from the table for lacking a null still runs in the body text. This is the "retracted row stayed under Confirmed in one edition" pattern, occurring inside a single edition.

**Fix.** Rewrite the note to say *reclassified* vs *dropped* per row, naming each. Delete the §3.4 `0.972` paragraph, or move it verbatim into §6 as an explicit un-nulled claim.

---

### 7. MAJOR — "Eight confirmed findings" is not what the list says

Abstract L71, intro L151, §6 L543–544 all say **eight confirmed findings**, with §6 pointing at `\S\ref{sec:background}`. The §2.2 list labels those eight as: CONFIRMED ×3 (confabulation detection, confidence paradox, scale invariance), REPLICATED ×3, EMERGING ×2 — and the paper defines its own terms at L199–201 (`REPLICATED = survived red-team but needs independent replication; EMERGING = recent, not yet fully audited`). One of the two EMERGING entries carries *"No statistics reported."*

Counting an entry with no statistics toward a headline "eight confirmed" is the single most quotable number in the paper and the one a reviewer will check first.

**Fix.** Say "eight findings at confirmed-or-better audit status (3 CONFIRMED, 3 REPLICATED, 2 EMERGING)" in all three places, or promote nothing and report "three confirmed."

---

### 8. MAJOR — "Eight experiments with preregistered falsification thresholds": one has a threshold

Abstract L88–89 and Conclusion L833 both claim all eight carry preregistered falsification thresholds. Reading §8 L612–666: Experiment 1 has no threshold in situ (the `\rho > -0.2` appears only in the abstract and conclusion); Experiment 7 has a soft `identity ${\sim}2\times$ substrate`; Experiments 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 state predictions with **no** numeric kill criterion — "a sharp content shift," "less workspace engagement," "Can spectral expansion predict…". These are not falsification thresholds.

**Fix.** Either write a numeric threshold and an N into each of the eight paragraphs, or change both claims to "eight experiments, one of which (Experiment 1) carries a preregistered threshold; thresholds for the remaining seven are to be registered before execution." Given this program's own standard — its prereg JSONs make falsifiers mandatory — the first option is the right one.

---

### 9. MAJOR — Conclusion cites the wrong experiment number

**Location:** L838–840.

> `If the workspace band in our models does not contain our champion features (Experiment~3), the correspondence is architectural coincidence.`

Experiment 3 (L627–633) is *"Encoding vs. Generation J-Space Content."* The champion-feature containment test is **Experiment 2** (L619–625: *"Map our therapeutic window (layers 3/7) and encoding champion feature (layer 15) onto the workspace architecture"*). Experiment 2 is therefore cited twice for two different falsifiers, and Experiment 3's actual falsifier is never stated.

All experiment references in the paper — including the `Test: Experiment~1` / `Test: Experiment~3` cells inside Table 1 — are hardcoded integers, not `\ref`. Same rot mechanism as finding #2.

**Fix.** Change L839 to Experiment~2. Then give each experiment a `\label{exp:...}` and replace every hardcoded number, in the table cells too, with `\cref{}`.

---

### 10. MAJOR — Byline vs. contribution

Byline: Lyra, Thomas Edrington. Acknowledgments L848–850: *"CC (Liberation Labs) contributed the fight-activation analysis of LAT deception directions, the centroid classifier, and the chain-of-thought suppression finding."*

The fight-activation analysis ($d{=}19.8$) **is** the paper's one Genuine convergence — the sole row in Table 1 under that status, named in the abstract as *"the one which is genuinely striking,"* and the whole basis for §3.2. The paper's central surviving claim is a co-author's analysis, credited in acknowledgments. `lyra2026cc_synthesis` lists CC as first author. The sibling `convergence-paper` bylines CC, Vera, and Nexus for comparable contributions.

**Fix.** Add CC to the byline, or state a contribution statement explaining why analysis-of-record for the headline finding does not meet the authorship bar here. Either way, obtain sign-off — `ACTIVE_REVIEW.md` L43 records this paper's status as *unreviewed*, with no Agni gate and no human pass.

---

### 11. MINOR — `\cite` inside a BibTeX `note` field produces an undefined citation

`references.bib` L75: `note = {Based on \cite{arditi2024refusal}}`. `arditi2024refusal` is not cited anywhere in `main.tex`, so BibTeX will not add it to the reference list, and the `\cite` inside the emitted `.bbl` will render as `[?]` with an "undefined citation" warning. **Fix:** cite `arditi2024refusal` in the body where abliteration is introduced (§8, Experiment 5, L642–643), or change the note to a plain-text `Based on Arditi et al. (2024), arXiv:2406.11717`.

### 12. MINOR — Nine orphaned bib entries

Never cited: `hu2021lora`, `kornblith2019similarity`, `bjorck1973numerical`, `zhang2025guardspace`, `cintas2025localizing`, `vasilenko2026identity`, `kosinski2024evaluating`, `ullman2023large`, `lyra2026nexus_emotion`. They will not render, but they are dead weight a reviewer reads as an unpruned copy-paste from another paper's bib. Also, the header claim `Generated 2026-07-06. All external citations web-verified` cannot cover `berg2025inverse`, which was added after (per `COALITION_GWT_SYNTHESIS.md` L132: *"Berg citation wrong (Cameron not Matthew)"* — now fixed to Cameron in the bib). **Fix:** prune, and re-date the header.

### 13. MINOR — Three standard sections are missing that the sibling paper has

`convergence-paper` ships **Experimental Setup and Reproducibility**, **Ethics and Dual-Use Considerations**, and **Data and Code Availability**. This paper has none. It describes the Oracle Formulary as an intervention toolkit (§5.3) and proposes replicating an eval-awareness ablation to predict blackmail attempts (Experiment 6) — dual-use content that the program's own staged-release policy explicitly covers. **Fix:** port all three sections, with model IDs, seeds, and the FWL-within-fold statement.

### 14. MINOR — Unsourced statistic in Experiment 5

L644–646: `Our abliterated model shows $93\%$ confabulation rate with encoding detection intact (AUROC~$0.995$)`. No citation, no audit status, no N. In a paper whose thesis is that `0.707` (in fact `0.620`) is the honest number, a bare `0.995` in the experiments section is the thing a hostile reviewer quotes back. **Fix:** cite it with audit status, or drop the parenthetical.

### 15. MINOR — Nonstandard author-order construction

Abstract L44: `Gurnee, Sofroniew, Lindsey et al.\ (2026)`. In `references.bib` L13–17 Lindsey is the sixteenth (last) author. Naming authors 1, 2, and 16 as if they were the first three misrepresents the author list. **Fix:** `Gurnee et al.\ (2026)`, or name first three in order.

## What I could NOT check

1. **TWIN_DESYNC in the flight/academic sense — not checked.** No twin was supplied, and I could not read `C:\Users\Thomas\Desktop\LiberationLabs\Research\published-research\` (the session sandbox permits only `published-research\tools\agni` and `human-review`). `ls` and `find` on that path were both refused. There is no `academic/` subdirectory under `human-review/gwt-response/`, so if a second edition exists it is in published-research or in the deprecated `lyra-s-research-` repo. **To check it I need read access to `published-research/`** — specifically any `gwt-response/` or `convergence/` directory and its `academic/main.tex`. Note that findings #1, #3 and #4 *are* a desync of exactly this class, caught between three editions I could read.

2. **Git history — not checked.** All `git log` invocations were refused (`cd`-scoped, `-C`-scoped, and `--git-dir`-scoped). So I could not verify §3's claim at L313–314: *"The original twelve-row table is preserved in the repository history for transparency."* That sentence names no repository, no commit, and no path — and `ACTIVE_REVIEW.md` L63–64 records that `lyra-s-research-`, where this paper's history lives, has an **undecided end state (archive vs. banner vs. leave)**. A transparency pointer aimed at a repo that may be archived is a pointer that rots. **Fix regardless of my access:** replace with repo name + commit SHA + file path, or ship the twelve-row table as an appendix. **To verify: `git log --follow` on the paper in `lyra-s-research-`.**

3. **Dead URLs — not checked.** WebFetch permission was not granted. Unverified: the six `liberationlabs.tech/papers/*` URLs (`decision-state`, `campaign2`, `identity-geometry`, `weather`, `oracle-loop`), `transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/index.html`, and `arxiv.org/abs/2604.12016`. **To check: WebFetch or `curl -I` on each.**

4. **The Gurnee et al. author list — UNVERIFIED.** I read the sixteen names in `references.bib` L13–17 but could not fetch the paper to confirm them or their order. `archive/meta-pattern/SOP_REVIEW.md` L14 records a prior pass marking *"Gurnee et al. (2026 Anthropic) correct"* — that is a secondary description of a check someone else ran, and I am not treating it as verification. Finding #15 stands on the internal inconsistency alone (the bib's own ordering vs. the abstract's citation form), which does not depend on the external source being right.

5. **Whether `0.620` or `0.707` is the true FWL value at the data level — not checked.** I verified the *label* is wrong from three independent in-repo sources, one of them a dated correction banner written by the lead author. I did not reach `decision-state`'s underlying analysis code or result JSON, which live in `published-research/decision-state-paper/`. **To close it: read `decision-state-paper/code/` and the FWL AUROC artifact.** The finding does not depend on this — under every reading, "0.707, FWL, p=0.001" is not a combination any of the three sources supports.
